entries.core_move: Classify a continuous-time input-output system as linear time-invariant by applying the superposition and time-shift tests together, establishing when the impulse-response and convolution framework applies.

entries.lesson_title: Why Linearity and Time Invariance Matter Together
entries.core_move: Justify why linearity and time invariance must be paired by tracing how shifted and scaled input components produce shifted and scaled copies of one reusable impulse response.
Interpret the unit impulse input $\delta$(t) as the canonical probe whose output from an LTI system becomes the reference response used for later shifted and scaled impulse inputs.
Determine an LTI system's impulse response $h(t)$ by evaluating its output to $\delta$(t) and interpreting that output as the kernel that governs shifted, scaled, and decomposed impulse inputs.

entries.lesson_title: Impulse Response as a System Description
entries.core_move: Use the impulse response $h(t)$ as a complete LTI-system description by mapping shifted and scaled impulse components to corresponding shifted and scaled copies of $h(t)$.

entries.lesson_title: Shifted Impulses Through an LTI System
entries.core_move: Map a shifted impulse input $\delta$(t - $\tau$) to the correspondingly shifted impulse response $h(t - \tau)$ by applying time invariance within the LTI impulse-response framework.

entries.lesson_title: Scaled Impulses Through an LTI System
entries.core_move: Compute the output of an LTI system for a scaled shifted impulse by applying homogeneity and time invariance to convert a $\delta$(t - t0) into a $h(t - t0)$.
